**Commentary of al-Tha'labi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 94, verses 1–8**

It is Meccan. It has one hundred and three letters, twenty-seven words, and eight verses.

Abu Muhammad Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad ibn Ali al-Jurjani informed us, saying: Abu al-Qasim Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim related to us, saying: Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Basri related to me, saying:

Muhammad ibn Abd al-Malik ibn Abi al-Shawarib related to us, saying: Abu Awana related to us, from Asim ibn Bahdala, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from Abd Allah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever recites *Did We not expand for you your breast?* (Alam Nashrah) is as if he came to me while I was distressed and relieved me." [174]

**In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful**

﴿Did We not expand for you your breast?﴾ Did We not open, widen, and soften your heart for you with faith, prophethood, knowledge, and wisdom?

﴿And We removed from you your burden, which had weighed down your back﴾ — "removed" means we lowered and set down; "burden" means we made heavy your back and weakened it. From this comes the expression for a camel that has been worn down by a journey and weakened: *naqd*. Al-Farra said: "It broke your back," on hearing its *naqid*, meaning its sound. Al-Hasan, Qatada, and al-Dahhak said: it means what had preceded from him in the pre-Islamic period of ignorance (jahiliyya). Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: it means error and forgetfulness. It was also said: it means the sins of your community, which He attributed to him because his heart was occupied with them and concerned for them. Abd al-Aziz ibn Yahya and Abu Ubayda said: it means He lightened for you the burdens of prophethood and the task of carrying out its affairs. It was also said: and He protected you from bearing the burden of sin.

﴿And We raised high for you your remembrance﴾

Abd al-Khaliq informed us by my reading to him, saying: Ibn Janb related to us, saying: Abu Isma'il Muhammad ibn Isma'il related to us, saying: Safwan, that is Ibn Salih al-Thaqafi Abu Abd al-Malik, related to us, saying: al-Walid, that is Ibn Muslim, related to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Lahi'a related to me, from Darraj, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he asked Jibril about this verse, *And We raised high for you your remembrance*. He said: "Allah, glorified is He, said: When you are remembered, I am remembered with you." [175] [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 30/297.]]

Abu Sa'id Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Uthman al-Wa'iz related to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Ahmad al-Jurjani related to us, saying: Imran ibn Musa informed us, saying: Abu Ma'mar related to us, saying: Abbad related to us, from Awf, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying *And We raised high for you your remembrance*, that he said: "When you are remembered, you are remembered with Me." Qatada said: Allah raises his remembrance in this world and the Hereafter, so there is no preacher, no one who recites the testimony, and no one who prays except that he calls out: "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." Mujahid said: it means the call to prayer (adhan), and Hassan ibn Thabit says in it, praising the Prophet (ﷺ):

*A radiant seal upon him for prophethood, from Allah, visible, shining and witnessing,*
*And the Lord joined the Prophet's name to His own name, when the muezzin says in the five prayers: "I bear witness."*
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/106.]]

Ibn Ata said: it means He made the completion of faith in Me depend upon your remembrance. It was also said: ﴿And We raised high for you your remembrance﴾ among the angels in the heavens. It was also said: through His taking the covenant from the prophets and obliging them to believe in him and to acknowledge his merit. Dhu al-Nun said: the aspirations of the prophets circulate around the Throne, but the aspiration of Muhammad (ﷺ) is above the Throne; therefore He said: *And We raised high for you your remembrance*, so his remembrance is his remembrance. The refuge of creation on the Day of Resurrection is to Muhammad (ﷺ), as their refuge is to Allah, because of their knowledge of his standing with Him.

﴿So indeed, with hardship there is ease﴾ — that is, with the hardship you are in, from fighting the polytheists and carrying out what you are engaged in, there is ease and relief, in that He will make you victorious over them, until they submit to the truth you have brought them, willingly or unwillingly.

﴿Indeed, with hardship there is ease﴾ — He repeated it to confirm the promise and magnify hope. It was also said: ﴿So indeed, with hardship there is ease﴾ refers to this world, and ﴿Indeed, with hardship there is ease﴾ refers to the Hereafter.

Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abd Allah related to us, saying: Uthman related to us, saying: Ibn Ulayya related to us, from Yunus, from al-Hasan, who said: When this verse was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Rejoice, for ease has come to you; hardship will never overcome two eases." [176] [[Sahih al-Bukhari: 6/87; Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 30/297.]]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Umar ibn al-Khattab related to us, saying: Ali ibn Mardaradh al-Khayyat related to us, saying: Qutn ibn Bashir related to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Sulayman related to us, from a man, from Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, who said:

Ibn Mas'ud said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, if hardship were in a hole, ease would seek it out until it entered upon it. Indeed, hardship will never overcome two eases. Indeed, hardship will never overcome two eases."

The scholars said regarding the meaning of this hadith: because he defined *hardship* with the definite article and made *ease* indefinite, and it is the custom of the Arabs that when you mention a definite noun and then repeat it, it is the same thing; and when you make it indefinite and then repeat it, they are two. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya ibn Nasr al-Jurjani, author of the book *al-Nazm*, said while speaking to people about the saying of the Prophet (peace be upon him), "Hardship will never overcome two eases" [177]: this yields nothing beyond their claim that *hardship* is definite and *ease* is indefinite and repeated; therefore *hardship* must be one and *ease* two. This is a flawed view, since in this kind of progression it does not follow: if a man says, "Indeed, with the horseman there is a sword; indeed, with the horseman there is a sword," it does not mean that the horseman is one and the swords are two. This is not valid in the composition of the Arabic language.

**A figurative reading (majaz)** of the saying: "Hardship will never overcome two eases."

Allah sent His Prophet (peace be upon him) poor and light in burden, so the polytheists reproached him for his poverty, until they said: "Shall we gather wealth for you?" He grieved, thinking they had denied him because of his poverty. So Allah, glorified and exalted is He, consoled him, enumerated His favors upon him, and promised him wealth. He said: ﴿Did We not expand for you your breast?﴾ up to His saying ﴿your remembrance﴾. This is the mention of His favor upon him. Then He began what He had promised him of wealth, to remove from his heart what had entered it, and He said: ﴿So indeed, with hardship there is ease﴾. The proof of this is the entry of the *fa'* (ف) in His saying *fa-inna* (فإن), and the *fa'* never enters except in a conjunction or as an answer.

Its figurative meaning: "Do not let what they say grieve you; indeed, with hardship there is ease in this world, swiftly." Then He fulfilled for him what He had promised, opened for him the Arab towns, and widened his means, so that he was given two hundred camels. Then He began another favor from the Hereafter, consoling him, saying: ﴿Indeed, with hardship there is ease﴾. The proof that it is a new beginning is that it is free of the *fa'* and the *waw* and the conjunctive particles. This is general for all believers. Its figurative meaning: "Indeed, with hardship in this world for the believers there is ease in the Hereafter, without doubt."

So the saying: "Hardship will never overcome two eases" means: the hardship of this world will not overcome the ease that Allah promised the believers in this world, and the ease that He promised them in the Hereafter. Only one of the two is overcome, namely the ease of this world. As for the ease of the Hereafter, it is lasting and does not cease; so the two do not combine in being overcome, just as his saying (peace be upon him) "Two feasts do not diminish" means they do not combine in diminishing.

Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: "With its sister in this world is the reward of Paradise." Al-Qasim said: [the coolness of this happiness from the dawns] of this world to the good pleasure of the final abode. [[Thus in the manuscript.]]

The common reading is with the two *sins* lightened (يُسْرًا, *yusran*). Abu Ja'far and Isa read them with the two letters vowelled (يُسُرًا, *yusuran*). In the reading of Abd Allah it is: "Indeed, with the hardship there is ease," once, not repeated.

Abu Abd al-Rahman Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ramjari and Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Baghdadi informed me, both saying: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Asamm related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Shaiban al-Ramli related to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Maymun al-Qaddah related to us, saying: Shihab ibn Khurrash related to us, from Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: A mule was presented as a gift to the Prophet (ﷺ), which Khosrow had given him. He rode it with a rope of hair, then he seated me behind him, and he traveled with me for a long time. Then he turned to me and said: "O boy." I said: "At your service, O Messenger of Allah." He said:

"Guard Allah and He will guard you. Guard Allah and you will find Him before you. Get to know Allah in ease and He will know you in hardship. When you ask, ask Allah; when you seek help, seek help from Allah. The pen has gone dry with what is to be. If all creation strove to benefit you with something Allah had not decreed for you, they would not be able to do it; and if they strove to harm you with something Allah had not written against you, they would not be able to do it. If you are able to act with patience together with certainty, then do so; if you are not able, then be patient, for in patience over what is disliked there is much good. Know that with patience comes victory, that with distress comes relief, and that *indeed, with hardship there is ease*." [178] [[With variation in Musnad Ahmad: 1/293; its complete form is in Kitab al-Du'a of al-Tabarani: 34.]]

I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Nisaburi say: I heard Abu Ali Muhammad ibn Amir al-Baghdadi say: I heard Abd al-Aziz ibn Yahya say: I heard my uncle say: I heard al-Utbi say: One day I was in the desert in a state of grief, and a line of verse came into my mind, so I said:

*I see death; I shall not rise in the morning, and I shall go to it grieved.*

When night fell I heard a caller calling from the air:

*O you person, whose worry has wearied him,*
*And who has recited a verse that keeps coming to his mind:*
*When hardship has pressed upon you, reflect on "Did We not expand for you your breast?"*
*Hardship lies between two eases; when you reflect upon them, rejoice.*

He said: So I memorized the verses, and Allah relieved my grief. [[Zad al-Masir: 8/273.]]

Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi recited to us, saying: Abu Muhammad Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Jizinjiyy recited to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Bahlul, the judge, recited to us:

*Do not despair, even if you become poor one day, for you will be made rich in a long age.*
*Do not think ill of your Lord, for Allah is more worthy of the good.*
*Indeed, hardship is followed by ease, and the word of Allah is truer than every word.* [[Husn al-Zann bi-Allah of Ibn Abi al-Dunya: 123; the verses are attributed there to Mahmud al-Warraq, with slight variation.]]

Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi also recited to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Sulayman ibn Mu'adh al-Karkhi recited to us, saying: Abu Bakr al-Anbari recited to us:

*When hardship reaches its utmost, then trust at that moment in swift ease.*
*Do you not see that the harshness of the winter's rain is followed by the spring's good fortune and beauty?*

And of Zayd ibn Muhammad al-Alawi:

*If time has struck you with affliction, the distress upon you has grown great and immense,*
*And calamities have followed it, weeping, so that you have grown weary of life and tired of it,*
*Then endure and await the end of it, for when calamities follow one another, they pass away.*
*And when they have weakened your strength and descended, they will uncover you wholly and withdraw.*

And another said:

*When misfortunes reach their limit and hearts almost melt from them,*
*And affliction descends and hope diminishes, then at the end comes relief.* [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 9/220.]]

Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Salusi recited to me, saying: Abu al-Hasan Isa ibn Zayd al-Aqili, the genealogist, recited to me, saying: Sulayman ibn Ahmad al-Raqqi recited to me:

*Expect, when calamities have befallen you, a joy that drives them away from you by force.*
*Do you see that Allah does not break His promise, and He has said: "Indeed, with hardship there is ease"?*

**So when you are free, labor (fanṣab)**

Ibn Abbas said: when you finish your prayer, *fa-nsab* — strive in supplication to your Lord, ask Him for your need, and turn to Him with desire.

Ibn Abi Najih related from Mujahid: when you rise for prayer, *fa-nsab* — strive in your need to your Lord.

Al-Dahhak said: when you finish the obligatory prayer, *fa-nsab* — strive in supplication to your Lord while you are seated before you give the salam.

Qatada said: He commanded him to strive greatly in his supplication when he finishes his prayer.

From al-Hasan: when you finish fighting your enemy, *fa-nsab* — strive in the worship of your Lord.

From Zayd ibn Aslam: when you finish fighting the Arabs and their fighting ends, *fa-nsab* — strive in the worship of Allah, and to Him *fa-rghab* — turn with desire.

From Mansur, from Mujahid: when you finish with the affairs of this world, *fa-nsab* — strive in the worship of your Lord and pray.

Muhammad ibn Abus informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hamim related to us, saying: al-Farra related to me, saying: Qays ibn al-Rabi' related to me, from Abu Husayn, who said: Shurayh passed by two men wrestling and said: "This is not what the one who is free is commanded to do. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: *So when you are free, labor, and to your Lord turn with desire.*" Al-Farra said: It is as though, in the saying of Shurayh, the one who is free is free from prayer or other things.

His saying *fa-nsab* is from *al-nasab*, which means weariness and perseverance in work. It was also said: He commanded him to sit for the tashahhud when he finishes the prayer, and to stand up for supplication. From Hayyan, from al-Kalbi: when you finish conveying the message, *fa-nsab*: that is, *istaghfir* — seek forgiveness for your sin and for the believers. From Junayd: when you finish with the affairs of creation, then strive in the worship of the Truth. From Abu al-Abbas ibn Ata: when you finish conveying the revelation, *fa-nsab* — strive in seeking intercession.

*And to your Lord turn with desire* — in all your states, not to anyone else. It was also said: when you finish with the preoccupations of this world, empty your heart for the concerns of the final abode.

From Ja'far: remember your Lord, being free from everything other than Him.

It was also said: when you finish worship, *fa-nsab* — turn away from it, fearing that it will be returned to you; *wa-ila rabbika fa-rghab* — and the seeking of forgiveness for your deed is like the shame of one who is bashful.

Shaykh Abu al-Fadl Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Khuza'i, the reciter, informed us, saying: Abu Muhammad Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Muzani related to us, saying: al-Walid ibn Bayyan, Yahya ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id, and Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Sataw related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Bura related to us, saying: Ikrima ibn Sulayman related to us, saying: I read to Isma'il ibn Abd Allah, and when I reached *Wa-l-Duha* he said: "Say *Allahu akbar* until we finish, along with the end of every surah, for I read to Shibl ibn Abbad and Ali ibn Abd Allah ibn Kathir, and they commanded me to do so."

He said: Abd Allah ibn Kathir informed me that he recited to Mujahid, and he commanded him to do so; Mujahid informed him that he recited to Ibn Abbas, and he commanded him to do so; Ibn Abbas informed him that he recited to Ubayy ibn Ka'b, and he commanded him to do so; Ubayy ibn Ka'b informed him that he recited to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he commanded him to do so.

[174]

*A radiant seal upon him for prophethood, from Allah, visible, shining and witnessing,*

**A figurative reading (majaz)** of the saying: "Hardship will never overcome two eases."

Allah sent His Prophet (peace be upon him) poor and light in burden, so the polytheists reproached him for his poverty, until they said: "Shall we gather wealth for you?" He grieved, thinking they had denied him because of his poverty. So Allah, glorified and exalted is He, consoled him, enumerated His favors upon him, and promised him wealth. He said: ﴿Did We not expand for you your breast?﴾ up to His saying ﴿your remembrance﴾. This is the mention of His favor upon him. Then He began what He had promised him of wealth, to remove from his heart what had entered it, and He said: ﴿So indeed, with hardship there is ease﴾. The proof of this is the entry of the *fa'* (ف) in His saying *fa-inna* (فإن), and the *fa'* never enters except in a conjunction or as an answer.

Its figurative meaning: "Do not let what they say grieve you; indeed, with hardship there is ease in this world, swiftly." Then He fulfilled for him what He had promised, opened for him the Arab towns, and widened his means, so that he was given two hundred camels. Then He began another favor from the Hereafter, consoling him, saying: ﴿Indeed, with hardship there is ease﴾. The proof that it is a new beginning is that it is free of the *fa'* and the *waw* and the conjunctive particles. This is general for all believers. Its figurative meaning: "Indeed, with hardship in this world for the believers there is ease in the Hereafter, without doubt."

So the saying: "Hardship will never overcome two eases" means: the hardship of this world will not overcome the ease that Allah promised the believers in this world, and the ease that He promised them in the Hereafter. Only one of the two is overcome, namely the ease of this world. As for the ease of the Hereafter, it is lasting and does not cease; so the two do not combine in being overcome, just as his saying (peace be upon him) "Two feasts do not diminish" means they do not combine in diminishing.

The scholars said regarding the meaning of this hadith: because he defined *hardship* with the definite article and made *ease* indefinite, and it is the custom of the Arabs that when you mention a definite noun and then repeat it, it is the same thing; and when you make it indefinite and then repeat it, they are two. **A figurative reading (majaz)** of the saying: "Hardship will never overcome two eases."

Allah sent His Prophet (peace be upon him) poor and light in burden, so the polytheists reproached him for his poverty, until they said: "Shall we gather wealth for you?" He grieved, thinking they had denied him because of his poverty. So Allah, glorified and exalted is He, consoled him, enumerated His favors upon him, and promised him wealth. He said: ﴿Did We not expand for you your breast?﴾ up to His saying ﴿your remembrance﴾. This is the mention of His favor upon him. Then He began what He had promised him of wealth, to remove from his heart what had entered it, and He said: ﴿So indeed, with hardship there is ease﴾. The proof of this is the entry of the *fa'* (ف) in His saying *fa-inna* (فإن), and the *fa'* never enters except in a conjunction or as an answer.

Its figurative meaning: "Do not let what they say grieve you; indeed, with hardship there is ease in this world, swiftly." Then He fulfilled for him what He had promised, opened for him the Arab towns, and widened his means, so that he was given two hundred camels. Then He began another favor from the Hereafter, consoling him, saying: ﴿Indeed, with hardship there is ease﴾. The proof that it is a new beginning is that it is free of the *fa'* and the *waw* and the conjunctive particles. This is general for all believers. Its figurative meaning: "Indeed, with hardship in this world for the believers there is ease in the Hereafter, without doubt."

So the saying: "Hardship will never overcome two eases" means: the hardship of this world will not overcome the ease that Allah promised the believers in this world, and the ease that He promised them in the Hereafter. Only one of the two is overcome, namely the ease of this world. As for the ease of the Hereafter, it is lasting and does not cease; so the two do not combine in being overcome, just as his saying (peace be upon him) "Two feasts do not diminish" means they do not combine in diminishing.

Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: "With its sister in this world is the reward of Paradise." Al-Qasim said: [the coolness of this happiness from the dawns] of this world to the good pleasure of the final abode. [[Thus in the manuscript.]]

When you ask, ask Allah; when you seek help, seek help from Allah. The pen has gone dry with what is to be. If all creation strove to benefit you with something Allah had not decreed for you, they would not be able to do it; and if they strove to harm you with something Allah had not written against you, they would not be able to do it. If you are able to act with patience together with certainty, then do so; if you are not able, then be patient, for in patience over what is disliked there is much good. Know that with patience comes victory, that with distress comes relief, and that *indeed, with hardship there is ease*." [178] [[With variation in Musnad Ahmad: 1/293; its complete form is in Kitab al-Du'a of al-Tabarani: 34.]]

I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Nisaburi say: I heard Abu Ali Muhammad ibn Amir al-Baghdadi say: I heard Abd al-Aziz ibn Yahya say: I heard my uncle say: I heard al-Utbi say: One day I was in the desert in a state of grief, and a line of verse came into my mind, so I said:

*I see death; I shall not rise in the morning, and I shall go to it grieved.*

When night fell I heard a caller calling from the air:

*O you person, whose worry has wearied him,*
*And who has recited a verse that keeps coming to his mind:*
*When hardship has pressed upon you, reflect on "Did We not expand for you your breast?"*
*Hardship lies between two eases; when you reflect upon them, rejoice.*

He said: So I memorized the verses, and Allah relieved my grief. [[Zad al-Masir: 8/273.]]

Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi recited to us, saying: Abu Muhammad Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Jizinjiyy recited to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Bahlul, the judge, recited to us:

*Do not despair, even if you become poor one day, for you will be made rich in a long age.*
*Do not think ill of your Lord, for Allah is more worthy of the good.*
*Indeed, hardship is followed by ease, and the word of Allah is truer than every word.* [[Husn al-Zann bi-Allah of Ibn Abi al-Dunya: 123; the verses are attributed there to Mahmud al-Warraq, with slight variation.]]

Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi also recited to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Sulayman ibn Mu'adh al-Karkhi recited to us, saying: Abu Bakr al-Anbari recited to us:

*When hardship reaches its utmost, then trust at that moment in swift ease.*
*Do you not see that the harshness of the winter's rain is followed by the spring's good fortune and beauty?*

And of Zayd ibn Muhammad al-Alawi:

*If time has struck you with affliction, the distress upon you has grown great and immense,*
*And calamities have followed it, weeping, so that you have grown weary of life and tired of it,*
*Then endure and await the end of it, for when calamities follow one another, they pass away.*
*And when they have weakened your strength and descended, they will uncover you wholly and withdraw.*

And another said:

*When misfortunes reach their limit and hearts almost melt from them,*
*And affliction descends and hope diminishes, then at the end comes relief.* [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 9/220.]]

Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Salusi recited to me, saying: Abu al-Hasan Isa ibn Zayd al-Aqili, the genealogist, recited to me, saying: Sulayman ibn Ahmad al-Raqqi recited to me:

*Expect, when calamities have befallen you, a joy that drives them away from you by force.*
*Do you see that Allah does not break His promise, and He has said: "Indeed, with hardship there is ease"?*

**So when you are free, labor (fanṣab)**

Ibn Abbas said: when you finish your prayer, *fa-nsab* — strive in supplication to your Lord, ask Him for your need, and turn to Him with desire.

Ibn Abi Najih related from Mujahid: when you rise for prayer, *fa-nsab* — strive in your need to your Lord.

Al-Dahhak said: when you finish the obligatory prayer, *fa-nsab* — strive in supplication to your Lord while you are seated before you give the salam.

Qatada said: He commanded him to strive greatly in his supplication when he finishes his prayer.

From al-Hasan: when you finish fighting your enemy, *fa-nsab* — strive in the worship of your Lord.

From Zayd ibn Aslam: when you finish fighting the Arabs and their fighting ends, *fa-nsab* — strive in the worship of Allah, and to Him *fa-rghab* — turn with desire.

From Mansur, from Mujahid: when you finish with the affairs of this world, *fa-nsab* — strive in the worship of your Lord and pray.

Muhammad ibn Abus informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hamim related to us, saying: al-Farra related to me, saying: Qays ibn al-Rabi' related to me, from Abu Husayn, who said: Shurayh passed by two men wrestling and said: "This is not what the one who is free is commanded to do. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: *So when you are free, labor, and to your Lord turn with desire.*" Al-Farra said: It is as though, in the saying of Shurayh, the one who is free is free from prayer or other things.

His saying *fa-nsab* is from *al-nasab*, which means weariness and perseverance in work. It was also said: He commanded him to sit for the tashahhud when he finishes the prayer, and to stand up for supplication. From Hayyan, from al-Kalbi: when you finish conveying the message, *fa-nsab*: that is, *istaghfir* — seek forgiveness for your sin and for the believers. *And to your Lord turn with desire* — in all your states, not to anyone else. It was also said: when you finish with the preoccupations of this world, empty your heart for the concerns of the final abode.

From Ja'far: remember your Lord, being free from everything other than Him.

It was also said: when you finish worship, *fa-nsab* — turn away from it, fearing that it will be returned to you; *wa-ila rabbika fa-rghab* — and the seeking of forgiveness for your deed is like the shame of one who is bashful.

**Commentary of al-Tha'labi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 94, verses 1–8**

It is Meccan. It has one hundred and three letters, twenty-seven words, and eight verses.

Abu Muhammad Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad ibn Ali al-Jurjani informed us, saying: Abu al-Qasim Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim related to us, saying: Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Basri related to me, saying:

Muhammad ibn Abd al-Malik ibn Abi al-Shawarib related to us, saying: Abu Awana related to us, from Asim ibn Bahdala, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from Abd Allah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever recites *Did We not expand for you your breast?* (Alam Nashrah) is as if he came to me while I was distressed and relieved me." [174]

**In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful**

﴿Did We not expand for you your breast?﴾ Did We not open, widen, and soften your heart for you with faith, prophethood, knowledge, and wisdom?

﴿And We removed from you your burden, which had weighed down your back﴾ — "removed" means we lowered and set down; "burden" means we made heavy your back and weakened it. From this comes the expression for a camel that has been worn down by a journey and weakened: *naqd*. Al-Farra said: "It broke your back," on hearing its *naqid*, meaning its sound. Al-Hasan, Qatada, and al-Dahhak said: it means what had preceded from him in the pre-Islamic period of ignorance (jahiliyya). Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: it means error and forgetfulness. It was also said: it means the sins of your community, which He attributed to him because his heart was occupied with them and concerned for them. Abd al-Aziz ibn Yahya and Abu Ubayda said: it means He lightened for you the burdens of prophethood and the task of carrying out its affairs. It was also said: and He protected you from bearing the burden of sin.

﴿And We raised high for you your remembrance﴾

Abd al-Khaliq informed us by my reading to him, saying: Ibn Janb related to us, saying: Abu Isma'il Muhammad ibn Isma'il related to us, saying: Safwan, that is Ibn Salih al-Thaqafi Abu Abd al-Malik, related to us, saying: al-Walid, that is Ibn Muslim, related to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Lahi'a related to me, from Darraj, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he asked Jibril about this verse, *And We raised high for you your remembrance*. He said: "Allah, glorified is He, said: When you are remembered, I am remembered with you." [175] [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 30/297.]]

Abu Sa'id Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Uthman al-Wa'iz related to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Ahmad al-Jurjani related to us, saying: Imran ibn Musa informed us, saying: Abu Ma'mar related to us, saying: Abbad related to us, from Awf, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying *And We raised high for you your remembrance*, that he said: "When you are remembered, you are remembered with Me." Qatada said: Allah raises his remembrance in this world and the Hereafter, so there is no preacher, no one who recites the testimony, and no one who prays except that he calls out: "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." Mujahid said: it means the call to prayer (adhan), and Hassan ibn Thabit says in it, praising the Prophet (ﷺ):

*A radiant seal upon him for prophethood, from Allah, visible, shining and witnessing,*
*And the Lord joined the Prophet's name to His own name, when the muezzin says in the five prayers: "I bear witness."*
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/106.]]

Ibn Ata said: it means He made the completion of faith in Me depend upon your remembrance. It was also said: ﴿And We raised high for you your remembrance﴾ among the angels in the heavens. It was also said: through His taking the covenant from the prophets and obliging them to believe in him and to acknowledge his merit. Dhu al-Nun said: the aspirations of the prophets circulate around the Throne, but the aspiration of Muhammad (ﷺ) is above the Throne; therefore He said: *And We raised high for you your remembrance*, so his remembrance is his remembrance. The refuge of creation on the Day of Resurrection is to Muhammad (ﷺ), as their refuge is to Allah, because of their knowledge of his standing with Him.

﴿So indeed, with hardship there is ease﴾ — that is, with the hardship you are in, from fighting the polytheists and carrying out what you are engaged in, there is ease and relief, in that He will make you victorious over them, until they submit to the truth you have brought them, willingly or unwillingly.

﴿Indeed, with hardship there is ease﴾ — He repeated it to confirm the promise and magnify hope. It was also said: ﴿So indeed, with hardship there is ease﴾ refers to this world, and ﴿Indeed, with hardship there is ease﴾ refers to the Hereafter.

Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abd Allah related to us, saying: Uthman related to us, saying: Ibn Ulayya related to us, from Yunus, from al-Hasan, who said: When this verse was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Rejoice, for ease has come to you; hardship will never overcome two eases." [176] [[Sahih al-Bukhari: 6/87; Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 30/297.]]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Umar ibn al-Khattab related to us, saying: Ali ibn Mardaradh al-Khayyat related to us, saying: Qutn ibn Bashir related to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Sulayman related to us, from a man, from Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, who said:

Ibn Mas'ud said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, if hardship were in a hole, ease would seek it out until it entered upon it. Indeed, hardship will never overcome two eases. Indeed, hardship will never overcome two eases."

The scholars said regarding the meaning of this hadith: because he defined *hardship* with the definite article and made *ease* indefinite, and it is the custom of the Arabs that when you mention a definite noun and then repeat it, it is the same thing; and when you make it indefinite and then repeat it, they are two. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya ibn Nasr al-Jurjani, author of the book *al-Nazm*, said while speaking to people about the saying of the Prophet (peace be upon him), "Hardship will never overcome two eases" [177]: this yields nothing beyond their claim that *hardship* is definite and *ease* is indefinite and repeated; therefore *hardship* must be one and *ease* two. This is a flawed view, since in this kind of progression it does not follow: if a man says, "Indeed, with the horseman there is a sword; indeed, with the horseman there is a sword," it does not mean that the horseman is one and the swords are two. This is not valid in the composition of the Arabic language.

**A figurative reading (majaz)** of the saying: "Hardship will never overcome two eases."

Allah sent His Prophet (peace be upon him) poor and light in burden, so the polytheists reproached him for his poverty, until they said: "Shall we gather wealth for you?" He grieved, thinking they had denied him because of his poverty. So Allah, glorified and exalted is He, consoled him, enumerated His favors upon him, and promised him wealth. He said: ﴿Did We not expand for you your breast?﴾ up to His saying ﴿your remembrance﴾. This is the mention of His favor upon him. Then He began what He had promised him of wealth, to remove from his heart what had entered it, and He said: ﴿So indeed, with hardship there is ease﴾. The proof of this is the entry of the *fa'* (ف) in His saying *fa-inna* (فإن), and the *fa'* never enters except in a conjunction or as an answer.

Its figurative meaning: "Do not let what they say grieve you; indeed, with hardship there is ease in this world, swiftly." Then He fulfilled for him what He had promised, opened for him the Arab towns, and widened his means, so that he was given two hundred camels. Then He began another favor from the Hereafter, consoling him, saying: ﴿Indeed, with hardship there is ease﴾. The proof that it is a new beginning is that it is free of the *fa'* and the *waw* and the conjunctive particles. This is general for all believers. Its figurative meaning: "Indeed, with hardship in this world for the believers there is ease in the Hereafter, without doubt."

So the saying: "Hardship will never overcome two eases" means: the hardship of this world will not overcome the ease that Allah promised the believers in this world, and the ease that He promised them in the Hereafter. Only one of the two is overcome, namely the ease of this world. As for the ease of the Hereafter, it is lasting and does not cease; so the two do not combine in being overcome, just as his saying (peace be upon him) "Two feasts do not diminish" means they do not combine in diminishing.

Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: "With its sister in this world is the reward of Paradise." Al-Qasim said: [the coolness of this happiness from the dawns] of this world to the good pleasure of the final abode. [[Thus in the manuscript.]]

The common reading is with the two *sins* lightened (يُسْرًا, *yusran*). Abu Ja'far and Isa read them with the two letters vowelled (يُسُرًا, *yusuran*). In the reading of Abd Allah it is: "Indeed, with the hardship there is ease," once, not repeated.
